messages:
incident-bot: INCIDENT ALERT — Increased 95th+ latency observed for 'economy' tier in us-east-1. Routing error rate up ~2.3%. Auto-pager: @maya_parker on-call. Please ack. :rotating_light:

maya_parker: acked. jumping in. checking dashboard now (https://console.redwood/metrics).

alan_sre: saw the spike — token processing time jump starting 00:09 UTC, correlates with a burst from a small group of customers hitting long-context prompts. P99 went 4x. No error-rate spike in dedicated pools.

jordan_ops: adding context: we deployed a routing weight change 00:06 to increase economy lane capacity for eu -> us-east overflow. Not sure if related.

emily_prod: @maya_parker do we have customer-facing impact? Any errors or just latency?

maya_parker: right now it's mostly latency; some timeouts reported by one enterprise customer (they're on economy fallback). Opening quick incident channel with CS. @cs_liaison can you reach out to the affected customer and tell them we're throttling gracefully?

cs_liaison: onboarding message sent to account team, they're aware. Asking for logs and example requests.

alan_sre: quick triage plan: 1) throttle top noisy clients via rate-limit overrides, 2) temporarily demote economy pref for specific busy request patterns, 3) throttle cross-region overflow routing (stop eu->us-east overflow).

kevin_eng: +1. I can push a targeted routing policy change. Suggest we reduce economy lane weight by 30% for us-east-1 and disable overflow routing for eu region for 15m. That should reduce queueing.

jordan_ops: implementing the overflow block now. Executing: 
```
# block eu->us-east overflow lane
curl -X POST https://ops-api/redwood/v1/routing/policies/modify \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer ****' \
  -d '{"action":"set_overflow","from_region":"eu-west-1","to_region":"us-east-1","enabled":false}'
```

incident-bot: Policy change requested by jordan_ops. Audit id: a1b2c3.

maya_parker: ok do it. jordan_ops please add an explicit TTL so we auto-revert if this prolongs.

jordan_ops: changed, TTL=900s (15m). Response: 200 OK, audit a1b2c3.

alan_sre: now throttling 3 heavy API keys at the edge. Using temporary quota caps: 40% of previous surge baseline. Command: 
```
# edge quota change
redis-cli -h quota-edge us set api_key:heavy123:rate_limit 0.4
```
Applied, keys show reduced throughput.

kevin_eng: I'm pushing a smart-routing reweight to bias traffic toward latency-optimized pool (reserved-capacity-1) for requests with short context <512 tokens. That should offload quick queries. Patch: 
```
PATCH /routing/weights HTTP/1.1
Host: ops-api
Content-Type: application/json
{
  "selector": {"max_context_len":512},
  "weights": {"reserved-capacity-1":0.7,"economy":0.3}
}
```

incident-bot: Change queued, will execute in 10s.

maya_parker: status? dashboards?

alan_sre: p99 dropping, now 1.6x baseline, errors stable. CPU on economy hosts down 20%.

emily_prod: any customer impact where requests were routed to lower-accuracy model variant? We changed weights.

kevin_eng: no model swap, just reweighting to different pools running the same model. Quality unchanged.

cs_liaison: customer from earlier confirmed improvement in retry rates, still seeing some slow tail for large contexts. They appreciated the proactive note.

maya_parker: good. next steps: keep overflow off, keep quota caps for noisy keys for 30m, monitor for 45m. Prepare rollback plan in case downstream latency appears.

jordan_ops: adding ephemeral policy to mute economy lane autoscaler to avoid aggressive spin-up. Command: 
```
POST /infra/autoscale/config
{"service":"economy-us-east","autoscale_override":"suspend","ttl":1800}
```

alan_sre: small caveat: suspending autoscale may increase queuing if we miscalculate — but given current burst source is cross-region overflow, it's fine short term.

emily_prod: can we add a rate-limit-by-pattern rule to reject extremely long-context requests in economy with a 429 and friendly message? That will protect tail latency.

kevin_eng: yes. Deploying rule: 
```
# reject long-context in economy
curl -X POST https://ops-api/rules -d '{"scope":"economy","condition":{"context_len":">2048"},"action":{"type":"reject","code":429,"message":"Please use dedicated or increase tier for long-context requests"}}'
```

incident-bot: Rule deployed, id r-9981.

maya_parker: monitoring the alerts: dashboards show steady improvement. P95 back to normal, P99 trending down. We'll leave mitigations for 30m and start gradual re-enable after 45m sanity window.

alan_sre: logging notes for postmortem: root cause likely combination of (a) routing weight change that increased eu->us-east overflow and (b) a small set of noisy API keys issuing long-context heavy prompts. Action items: automated detection for long-tail cross-region bursts + autopruning fallback policies.

jordan_ops: audit entries: overflow disable a1b2c3, quota caps qcap-235, autoscale suspend auto-345, long-context reject r-9981.

cs_liaison: customers notified. No major SLA breaches reported so far. One enterprise sent a few 504s but accepted workaround.

maya_parker: handing back to normal ops. I'll leave a short runbook update: add an entry under 'regional-shaping' that describes this exact mitigation set (overflow toggle, quota caps, reweight short-context -> reserved pool).

kevin_eng: I'll open a quick PR with the runbook and a drafted detection alert for cross-region long-context surges.

maya_parker: thanks everyone. closing thread when metrics stable for 1h. :white_check_mark:
